advances: The original-mean logarithmic hitting argument extends to every real coupling matrix on the unchanged free-sum support. The real-shift partition loss is absorbed by the existing second-block factor in \(2^n\), giving coefficient \(1/48\). For every actual convex body with this complete volume table up to common positive scaling, the original root-hitting consumer supplies one point in its original fiber at zero with depth coefficient \(1/288\), in its actual continuous dimension. Every such scalar table also has explicit support-preserving convex-body approximations with a quantitative depth bound at the same integer center, without a mean assumption on the perturbed tables. This proves the bridge for the stated class of coupled convex potentials and includes exactly stationary scalar examples with irrational coupling and their actual convex-body approximations.

Accepted fact `cd6a1446e7ce3997` supplies the geometric notation, auxiliary first-block law, central-pair mechanism, and finite-moment construction pattern; their needed subclaims are verified here for the present real coupling. Accepted fact `f55232eea7862d8c` supplies (7) for every real shift and the exact absorption used in (14). Accepted fact `488f0a583886b5fc` supplies the canonical logarithmic normalization, equality of the arbitrary-support and independent-support hitting formulations, cutoff attainment, and the explicit convex-roof realization with its pointwise-in-center support and capacity comparisons. Accepted fact `7fa5a28fe1ac6893` supplies the actual-body nonnegativity of root costs and the attained original-fiber depth bound for all closed ambient halfspaces. The new subprobability comparison, original-law cancellation, stationary irrational example, original-table scaling and eligibility maps, and fixed-center composition with the approximation bounds are proved above.
statement:
Let \(r,s,h_x,h_y\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), put \(n=r+s\), and let \(a\ge0\) and \(B\in\mathbb R^{s\times r}\). Retain the geometric notation of accepted fact `cd6a1446e7ce3997`:

\[
\begin{aligned}
R&=\operatorname{conv}\bigl([0,h_x]^r\cup\{-\mathbf1_r\}\bigr),
&Q&=[-h_y,h_y]^s,\\
P&=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((R\times\{\mathbf0\})\cup(\{\mathbf0\}\times Q)\bigr),
&D&=P\cap\mathbb Z^n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]

Write \(\mathbf I=(x,y)\in\mathbb Z^r\times\mathbb Z^s\). Let \(V:R\to\mathbb R\) be finite and convex, with \(V(\mathbf0)=0\), and define the original potential and complete table by

\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi(x,y)&=V(x)+a\|y-Bx\|_\infty\quad((x,y)\in P),
&\phi_{\mathbf I}&=\phi(x,y),\\
w_{\mathbf I}&=e^{-\phi_{\mathbf I}}\quad(\mathbf I\in D),
&w_{\mathbf I}&=0\quad(\mathbf I\notin D),
&W&=\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}w_{\mathbf I}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]

Assume the original weighted mean is \(\mathbf J_0=W^{-1}\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}w_{\mathbf I}\mathbf I=\mathbf0\). The support, indices, and weights in this hypothesis are exactly (1)-(2). In particular, \(B\) may have arbitrary irrational entries.

For \(L\ge0\), use the original full-capacity logarithmic hitting quantity of accepted fact `488f0a583886b5fc`. Explicitly, a barycentric support at \(\mathbf0\) consists of a nonempty \(E\subseteq D\) and positive coefficients \(\lambda_{\mathbf I}\) satisfying \(\sum_E\lambda_{\mathbf I}=1\) and \(\sum_E\lambda_{\mathbf I}\mathbf I=\mathbf0\). Its gap is \(G_\lambda=\sum_E\lambda_{\mathbf I}\phi_{\mathbf I}-\phi_{\mathbf0}\). Define \(m_{\log}(\mathbf0,L;w)\) to be the minimum of \(\sum_{\mathbf I\in F}w_{\mathbf I}\) over subsets \(F\subseteq D\) meeting every such support with \(G_\lambda\le L\). Each selected source is charged its full original weight. The accepted fact identifies this definition with its finite family \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf0}\) of affinely independent supports, equipped with their unique positive barycentric coefficients. All cutoff inequalities include equality.

The objects \(n,P,D,w,W\) have their canonical meanings in `488f0a583886b5fc`. Our normalization is \(\phi_{\mathbf0}=0\), so that fact's normalized potential is \(\phi_{\mathbf I}-\min_D\phi\), and its \(w_{\max}\) is \(e^{-\min_D\phi}\). These substitutions preserve every weight and every gap. Its scalar amplitude called \(B\) would be \(\max_D\phi-\min_D\phi\); it is distinct from the coupling matrix in (2). The geometric objects and the first-block meaning of \(V\) agree with `cd6a1446e7ce3997`, while the table (2) uses the present real matrix.

The exact complete support, including boundary sites, is

\[
D=\{(-\mathbf1_r,\mathbf0)\}
\cup\left\{(x,y):
x\in\{0,\ldots,h_x\}^r,\quad y\in\mathbb Z^s,\quad
\frac{\|x\|_\infty}{h_x}+\frac{\|y\|_\infty}{h_y}\le1
\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]

The table is globally extendable in the sense of `488f0a583886b5fc`, \(P=\operatorname{conv}D\) has dimension \(n\), \(\mathbf0\in\operatorname{int}P\), and \(w_{\mathbf0}=1\). Put \(\gamma=2/\sqrt3\) and \(Z_{\mathrm{cube}}=\sum_{y\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^s}e^{-a\|y\|_\infty}=\sum_{y\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^s}w_{(\mathbf0,y)}\). Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
W&\le 2^{r+1}\,2\gamma^s Z_{\mathrm{cube}},\\
m_{\log}(\mathbf0,4s;w)&\ge\frac{Z_{\mathrm{cube}}}{4},\\
\max_{L\ge0}\frac{m_{\log}(\mathbf0,L;w)}{1+L}
&\ge\frac{m_{\log}(\mathbf0,4s;w)}{1+4s}
\ge\frac{W}{48\,2^n}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

For an explicit stationary irrational family, take \(r=2\), \(s=1\), \(B=(\sqrt2,-\sqrt2)\), any integers \(h_x,h_y\ge2\), and any \(a>0\). There is a finite convex \(V\), constructed in the proof, with \(V(\mathbf0)=0\) and exactly the original mean \(\mathbf J_0=\mathbf0\). The resulting potential values on \(D\) cannot be expressed as \(U(x)+T(y)\) for functions on the corresponding projections of \(D\).

For the actual-body conclusion, let \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) be any continuous dimension, independently of \(r,s\). Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, let \(C_{\mathbf I}=\{z\in\mathbb R^d:(\mathbf I,z)\in C\}\), and suppose that some \(\alpha>0\) gives the complete volume table

\[
w^C_{\mathbf I}:=\mathcal L^d(C_{\mathbf I})=\alpha w_{\mathbf I}
\qquad\text{for every }\mathbf I\in\mathbb Z^n.
\tag{5}
\]

This equality includes all zero-volume fibers. Put \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d\), \(S=C\cap\Lambda\), and \(W_C=\mathcal H_d(S)=\alpha W\). There exists one \(z^\star\in C_{\mathbf0}\) such that every closed ambient halfspace \(H\) containing \((\mathbf0,z^\star)\) satisfies

\[
\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\ge\frac{W_C}{288\,2^n},
\qquad
h_S((\mathbf0,z^\star))\ge\frac{W_C}{288\,2^n}.
\tag{6}
\]

Here \(h_S\) is exactly the locked closed-halfspace depth. In applying accepted fact `7fa5a28fe1ac6893`, its \(C,S,\Lambda,n,d\) are these actual objects, its \(D\) is (3), its weights and total are \(w^C\) and \(W_C\), and its target \(\mathbf J\) is \(\mathbf0\). Its continuous fiber variable is denoted \(z\) here, whereas \(y\) is the second integer block. Its roots \(a_{\mathbf I}\) are \((w^C_{\mathbf I})^{1/d}\), distinct from the coefficient \(a\) in (2), and its \(\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d\) is distinct from \(\gamma=2/\sqrt3\). Its hitting mass \(m_d(\mathbf J,L)\) will be written \(m_d(\mathbf0,L;w^C)\) to display the original target and capacities.

There are also explicit actual-body approximations for every scalar table satisfying (1)-(2) and the original-mean hypothesis, including the irrational family. Put \(w_{\max}=e^{-\min_D\phi}\), \(\psi_{\mathbf I}=\phi_{\mathbf I}-\min_D\phi\), and \(\beta=\max_D\psi\). The new symbols \(\psi\) and \(\beta\) distinguish the normalized potential and scalar amplitude from the origin-normalized \(\phi\) and matrix \(B\). Let

\[
\widehat\psi(\xi)=\min\left\{
\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}\lambda_{\mathbf I}\psi_{\mathbf I}:
\lambda_{\mathbf I}\ge0,\quad\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}\lambda_{\mathbf I}=1,\quad
\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}\lambda_{\mathbf I}\mathbf I=\xi
\right\}\qquad(\xi\in P).
\]

For every integer \(q>\beta\), define

\[
\begin{aligned}
C^{(q)}&=\left\{(\xi,z)\in P\times\mathbb R^q:
0\le z_j\le w_{\max}^{1/q}(1-\widehat\psi(\xi)/q)
\quad(1\le j\le q)\right\},\\
w^{(q)}_{\mathbf I}&=
\begin{cases}
w_{\max}(1-\psi_{\mathbf I}/q)^q,&\mathbf I\in D,\\
0,&\mathbf I\notin D,
\end{cases}
&W^{(q)}&=\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}w^{(q)}_{\mathbf I},\\
\kappa_q&=1-\beta/q,
&\varepsilon_q&=-q\log(1-\beta/q)-\beta.
\end{aligned}
\]

Then \(C^{(q)}\) is a full-dimensional compact convex polytope in \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^q\), and \(w^{(q)}\) is its complete integer-fiber volume table. In particular the integer dimension and positive support remain exactly \(n\) and \(D\). Put \(\Lambda^{(q)}=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^q\) and \(S^{(q)}=C^{(q)}\cap\Lambda^{(q)}\), so \(W^{(q)}=\mathcal H_q(S^{(q)})\). There exists one \(z_q^\star\in C^{(q)}_{\mathbf0}\), selected before the halfspace, such that every closed ambient halfspace \(H\) containing \((\mathbf0,z_q^\star)\) satisfies

\[
\mathcal H_q(S^{(q)}\cap H)
\ge e^{-\varepsilon_q}
\max\left\{\kappa_q,\frac1{1+\varepsilon_q}\right\}
\frac{W^{(q)}}{288\,2^n}.
\]

No original-mean condition is imposed on \(w^{(q)}\); the integer center in this conclusion is still \(\mathbf0\). The coefficient multiplying \(W^{(q)}/(288\,2^n)\) tends to one as \(q\to\infty\). For this approximation application of `488f0a583886b5fc`, its normalized \(\phi\), roof \(\widehat\phi\), scalar amplitude \(B\), and constructed continuous dimension \(q\) map respectively to \(\psi,\widehat\psi,\beta,q\) here. Its \(n,D,P,w,w_{\max}\) remain those of the original scalar table. When `7fa5a28fe1ac6893` is applied to these new bodies, its \(C,S,\Lambda,d,w,W\) instead map to \(C^{(q)},S^{(q)},\Lambda^{(q)},q,w^{(q)},W^{(q)}\); its integer dimension is still \(n\), target still \(\mathbf0\), and roots are \((w^{(q)}_{\mathbf I})^{1/q}\). This explicitly constructed continuous dimension \(q\) is independent of the actual dimension \(d\) in the conditional conclusion (5)-(6).
